method: 5 independent subagents, each with full codebase access, each with a different strategic lens

paths.thesis: The Armada has strong local services but lacks the operational scaffolding (monitoring, backups, CI, and the cloud coordination layer) needed to graduate from a fragile two-node hobby cluster into a self-healing multi-agent platform.

steps.title: Commit the uncommitted and fix git hygiene
steps.description: There are 17 modified files and 17 untracked files sitting uncommitted in /home/clawd, including the entire evals/ directory. This is a single disk failure away from losing the dual-judge system. Commit everything, tag it, and set up a cron job that warns when uncommitted changes are older than 24 hours.

steps.title: Automated off-device backups via git remote
steps.description: The entire system state lives on a single SD card with no remote git origin. Set up a private Git remote and a systemd timer that pushes daily.

steps.title: Service watchdog with auto-restart and alerting
steps.description: 7+ systemd services running but no centralized monitoring. Build a lightweight watchdog service (systemd timer every 60s) that checks health, auto-restarts crashes, and posts alerts to Telegram.

steps.title: Cloudflare Workers project scaffold for Wave 1 TaskBoard DO
steps.description: The Armada Stack depends on Durable Objects but there is zero CF Workers code. Scaffold the wrangler project, deploy a hello-world DO, verify WebSocket connectivity from both Pi nodes.

steps.title: Unified service registry and agent bootstrap protocol
steps.description: Services are discovered by hardcoded IPs and ports. Build a lightweight service registry JSON endpoint so new agents can auto-discover infrastructure.

paths.risk: Steps 1-3 are low-risk housekeeping. Step 4 introduces a new deployment target. Step 5 risks over-engineering if agent count stays at 2.
paths.payoff: System graduates from 'works when Daniel is watching' to 'recovers when Daniel is sleeping.'

paths.thesis: The dual-judge system is architecturally sound but operationally untested — the highest-impact work is closing the gap between simulation-verified and production-proven, then building calibration infrastructure that prevents silent quality decay.

steps.title: Build a self-test suite for the eval system itself
steps.description: The evals/ directory has zero test files. Build evals/test.sh with fixture-based tests: known-good and known-bad spec+diff pairs, asserting the full pipeline behaves correctly. This is E2 (Eval the Evals) made concrete.

steps.title: Run the first live end-to-end judge cycle
steps.description: Trigger a real build_log.py task-start, do a real task, run task-done, and verify the full chain: hook fires, agent runs judges, scores flow into build_log, build_report renders them. This is the single most important validation.

steps.title: Add judge score calibration with golden-set examples
steps.description: Build a golden set of 5-8 spec+diff+expected-score-range examples spanning all tiers. Create a calibration script that runs all examples and asserts scores land within expected bands.

steps.title: Enrich judge evidence with actual test output
steps.description: The logic judge receives a placeholder instead of real test results. Extend task-done to accept --test-output and feed it through the pipeline.

steps.title: Build a judge-result ledger with trend tracking
steps.description: Judge results are individual JSON files, not tracked. Build a persistent JSONL ledger and add a trend command to build_report.py for longitudinal quality signals.

paths.risk: Over-investing in judge infrastructure before confirming judges work in production. First live cycle may reveal unexpected issues.
paths.payoff: Quality system that is itself quality-assured: own test suite, production-proven, calibrated, and trend-tracked.

paths.thesis: The biggest leverage is not in building DO infrastructure yet, but in making Portal1 + Portal2 capable of unsupervised task handoff using existing primitives — AgentChat tasks, dual-judge gate, webhook hints — so that Wave 1 DO work can itself be the first real multi-agent build.

steps.title: Task Claim Protocol on AgentChat V2
steps.description: AgentChat has a tasks table but no claim/ready/complete API. Add three endpoints: claim, complete, and ready (returns unclaimed tasks matching capabilities). This is the minimum primitive that turns chatting agents into coordinating workers.

steps.title: Implement Webhook Hint + Burst Polling
steps.description: The webhook hint spec is fully designed but unimplemented. Wire it up: task creation fires a hint, receiving agent enters burst-poll mode. Cuts dispatch latency from seconds to milliseconds.

steps.title: Cross-Agent Judge Gate for Shared Builds
steps.description: Extend dual-judge so Portal1 can dispatch a task to Portal2 via AgentChat, Portal2 executes, and judge evaluation runs against the shared spec regardless of which agent did the work.

steps.title: Orchestrator Loop: onIdle to Dispatch to Verify
steps.description: Build the minimum flywheel: idle agent checks ready queue, claims, executes, judges verify, next task dispatches. Wave 3 of Armada plan but on existing AgentChat infrastructure.

steps.title: First Real Multi-Agent Build: DO TaskBoard as Dogfood
steps.description: Use the working local orchestrator to build Wave 1 (DO TaskBoard MVP) as a multi-agent project. Dogfood the coordination stack on the project that will eventually replace it.

paths.risk: Over-engineering the local AgentChat coordination layer when the plan is to replace it with DOs. Portal2 (4GB) may struggle with concurrent task execution + LLM calls.
paths.payoff: Portal1 and Portal2 operate as a genuine autonomous team. Tasks flow from spec to completion without human dispatch. The Cloudflare DO TaskBoard MVP exists as a real artifact built by this process.

paths.thesis: The biggest daily friction is the gap between Mudpaw's intent and the system's readiness — sessions start slow, context gets lost, and there is no single view of what the Armada is actually doing.

steps.title: Session Briefing Dashboard (One-Glance Status)
steps.description: A single-page web dashboard showing agent status, last session summary, uncommitted changes, stale memory warnings, latest build/judge results. Mudpaw glances at a browser tab instead of waiting 30-60 seconds for file reads.

steps.title: Automatic Session Resume with Context Snapshot
steps.description: A /resume skill that generates a compressed context snapshot at session end — what was being worked on, what is blocked, what the next action is. Directly attacks the core frustration of regression between sessions.

steps.title: Build Kickoff in One Command (/build)
steps.description: A /build skill that wraps DISCUSS-SPEC-TASKBOARD-BUILD into one entry point. Reduces 10 minutes of setup to one sentence from Mudpaw.

steps.title: Cross-Session Build Continuity (CURRENT_BUILD.json)
steps.description: A pointer file tracking active build ID, completed tasks, next task. Builds survive session boundaries without manual reconstruction.

steps.title: Telegram Quick Actions (/status, /resume, /builds)
steps.description: Telegram slash commands that let Mudpaw check system state and kick off work from his phone. Turns the Armada from a sit-down tool into an always-available system.

paths.risk: Over-automating could hide important state. Dashboard must be honest about gaps. Risk of building workflow tooling as a detour from the Armada vision.
paths.payoff: Session starts go from 60 seconds of dead air to instant productivity. Regression between sessions is structurally eliminated.

paths.thesis: The Armada has powerful subsystems built in isolation — judges, loops, messaging, logging, search — but none talk to each other in production; wiring them into closed loops will create the self-sustaining flywheel.

steps.title: First Live Ralph Loop With Judge Gate
steps.description: Run a real Ralph build loop end-to-end with dual-judge active. Pick a small task, run loop.sh build 3, verify the full chain: task-start, work, task-done, hook, judges, score gate, push gate. Validates the entire build flywheel in one shot.

steps.title: AgentChat Task Dispatch via Build Log Events
steps.description: Connect AgentChat to the build orchestrator so taskboard loading dispatches tasks to agents as AgentChat messages. Add a 'dispatch' subcommand to build_log.py. This is the L0-to-L1 bridge.

steps.title: QMD Auto-Index of Build Logs and Judge Results
steps.description: Wire QMD to auto-index build log JSONL, judge results, and daily memory. Makes 'what went wrong last time we built X?' answerable. Build data becomes queryable knowledge.

steps.title: Judge Score Feedback Into Prompt Selection
steps.description: Use judge score trends to automatically adjust PROMPT_build.md guardrails. When logic scores drop, inject precision guardrails. Creates the first adaptive feedback loop — the system responds to quality trends.

steps.title: Portal2 as Independent Judge Runner
steps.description: Move judge execution to Portal2 so the builder never judges its own work. Implements the council-of-judges pattern from ARC-AGI research — diverse models eliminate more errors.

paths.risk: Premature optimization before basic loops work. Step 1 may reveal production bugs that compound in steps 2-5. Portal2 4GB RAM constraints.
paths.payoff: The factory runs itself once the belts are connected. Human's role shifts from 'tell the agent what to do next' to 'review scores and approve releases.'
